title: SLI decomposition catalog and trace atlas
body:
Purpose:
This is a working artifact for breaking down high-level SLIs into measurable components (decomposition), mapping those components to trace annotations, and then proposing a compact dashboard (trace atlas) for fast investigation. Goal: reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) for token-latency incidents and make KV-cache/cold-start signal actionable.

Scope:
- Inference text-generation and chat routes (hosted + dedicated)
- Both multi-tenant and dedicated pools (tenant isolation signals included)
- Focus on first-response latency (TTFT) and tail latency (95/99/99.9) decomposition

Key definitions (canonical):
1) SLI: request_first_token_latency_ms = time from request-ingest to first-token-emitted (client-visible).
   - Instrument points: http_ingest_ts, scheduling_enqueue_ts, scheduling_dequeue_ts, dispatch_to_gpu_ts, kv_lookup_start, kv_lookup_end, first_token_emit_ts.
2) backend_compute_ms = dispatch_to_gpu_ts -> first_token_emit_ts (includes KV wait when blocking).
3) kv_latency_ms = kv_lookup_end - kv_lookup_start (if present; null if cache-miss/non-blocking).
4) scheduling_queue_ms = scheduling_dequeue_ts - scheduling_enqueue_ts.
5) user_perceived_tail = 95/99/99.9 quantiles on request_first_token_latency_ms partitioned by model, route, tenant_tier.

SLI decomposition examples (how to attribute a 2.2s first-token):
- scheduling_queue_ms: 1200ms (high queueing during burst)
- kv_latency_ms: 600ms (blocking KV fetch + remote cold)
- backend_compute_ms: 300ms (GPU time)
- misc (serialization, network): 100ms
Notes: if kv_latency_ms is >50% of first_token_latency, mark incident as "cold-cache" and trigger KV warmup playbook.

Trace annotation schema (proto / key names to add to spans):
- span.kind = "ingest" / "scheduler" / "dispatch" / "gpu_op" / "kv" / "emit"
- attrs: request_id, tenant_id, model_name, model_version, route, seq_len_in, seq_len_out, kv_key_presence (hit|miss|stale), preempted (true|false), batching_id, batch_size
- numeric attrs: token_index, gpu_index, queue_position

Sampling & retention policy (proposal):
- Always-sample: requests with first_token_latency > 500ms OR kv_latency_ms > 200ms OR 99.9 quantile contributors.
- Rate-sample: 1% baseline across all traffic to maintain coverage for low-volume models.
- Priority retention window: hot traces kept 14d; baseline traces 7d; aggregated span histograms retained 90d.

Dashboard (trace atlas) plan — compact widgets mapped to decomposition: (widget_id: short query description)
- W1: First-token latency heatmap (by model, route) -- shows p50/p95/p99 over last 1h in 1m buckets.
- W2: Decomposition stacked bars (queue | kv | compute | misc) -- per-route 5m rollup.
- W3: KV hit-rate + conditional kv_latency_ms distribution -- partition by tenant_tier.
- W4: Tail-trace quicklinks -- top anomalous request_ids with direct link to trace viewer.
- W5: Probe vs real-traffic delta (synthetic probe latency vs production) to detect cold-start regime.
- W6: Batch-size distribution and correlation with first-token latency.

Alerting heuristics (early-warning):
- Alert A: p99_first_token_latency > 1200ms for 5m AND p99_increase >= 30% vs baseline -> Severity P1.
- Alert B: proportion_of_requests_with_kv_latency>200ms > 5% in last 10m -> P2 (investigate cache priming).
- Alert C: scheduling_queue_ms median > 300ms AND backend_utilization > 85% -> auto-scale recommended.

Owner & handoff:
- Observability team maintains metric contracts and trace annotation proto.
- Serving-runtime owns dispatch and gpu_op spans.
- Platform infra owns scheduling queue metrics and autoscaler hooks.

Runbook snippets (for oncall):
1) Confirm: is p99 elevated globally or scoped to model/route/tenant? Use W1 + W2.
2) If kv signal high: check W3, search traces for span.kind=kv, filter kv_key_presence=miss. If confirmed, trigger KV warmup job and mark rollout flag.
3) If queueing dominant: check autoscaler logs + W6, consider immediate scale or backpressure.
4) If GPU compute dominant: pull top traces (W4), correlate with batch size; check for recent quantization/compile rollouts.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Define exact numeric sampling thresholds for low-volume models (propose 5 traces/hr).
- [ ] Add tenant-anonymized stack to traces for privacy (PHI-safe mode).
- [ ] Finalize retention tiers with storage team (cost estimates attached in INF-4123).
- [ ] Create a lightweight dashboard-mobile layout for oncall quick triage.

References & links:
- Confluence: metric-registry-v2 (see linked_artifacts)
- Jira: INF-4123 (sampling + retention)
summary: Decomposition catalog + trace annotation proposal to drive a compact dashboard and faster MTTR for token latency incidents (draft).
